title: Freeze recovery inventory class contract and quarantine record
description: Objective: resolve the current contradictory inventory cardinality and define the durable fail-closed reconciliation/quarantine record the coordinator can persist. Deliverable: one canonical daemon recovery-inventory contract that maps every detailed external population to exactly one configured proof class, defines ABSENT/ADOPTED/QUARANTINED/UNKNOWN dispositions and upstream-code retention, and provides a frozen digest-verified persisted record bound to project, backup cursor/generation, selected incarnation/key epoch and quarantine refs. MEASURED GAP at HEAD c0c5929: design line 978 names seven populations, CORE-S14 names six grouped categories, @moe/runner exposes four combined node classes, adding scheduler resource yields five proof classes, the coordinator description lists six groups, and DoD demands seven generated classes; the runner collector rejects unknown/extra classes. No production quarantine/reconciliation record or sink exists. Consumer: task-cf7fb147bd1c47698cbd65c9535370aa and downstream task-6f786c58cabf4f85be8ed4135e68a752. NOT in scope: enumerating providers, invoking adapters, allocating authority, or approving recovery.complete. Owned paths: focused daemon recovery contract/codec/persistence modules and tests, plus minimal store schema only if required. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm --filter @moe/store test.
definitionOfDone: A frozen hand-written class/population mapping resolves the 4-runner/5-proof/6-scenario/7-population ambiguity: every design population is covered exactly once, no proof is duplicated to inflate cardinality, and unknown/duplicate/omitted/extra classes refuse with stable code/layer.

The contract defines canonical ABSENT, ADOPTED, QUARANTINED and UNKNOWN dispositions; ADOPTED requires exact restored intent plus current incarnation/key epoch, unmatched items can only quarantine/UNKNOWN, and no disposition invents history or retry authority.

A durable frozen reconciliation record binds project, backup cursor and generation, selected incarnation and key epoch, configured class mapping, source proof digests, every item disposition, retained upstream code/layer and quarantine refs; any byte change changes or invalidates its digest.

Missing inventory, incomplete coverage, non-fenceable state, artifact/key proof failure and unresolved items persist truth UNKNOWN with coordinator code UNKNOWN_TRUTH at RECOVERY_INVENTORY while retaining the precise upstream code/layer separately.
Persistence/reopen and hostile-byte tests drive the real store/codec surface, assert exact cardinalities and stable code/layer, and generated cases assert a non-zero exact population count.

Mutation drills alter canonical digest input and one adoption/incarnation comparison and turn named tests red; fresh pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm --filter @moe/store test exits 0.
taskRails: Do not satisfy the seven-population requirement by duplicating a combined runner proof; the mapping must be explicit and one-to-one at the semantic population level.
Do not narrow the design or accept caller-selected current binding; use exact selected store/anchor authority in consumers.
Retain upstream code and layer separately from the coordinator UNKNOWN_TRUTH/RECOVERY_INVENTORY answer; never restamp away provenance.
Shared schema changes require full regression and crash/reopen evidence.
Target <=250 physical lines per production source and split before 400; the cap is per file.

implementationPlan.description: Implement the focused contract and exact LF NodeNext bridge. Freeze ordered proof classes as `PROVIDER_PROCESS_LAUNCH_LOCK`, `RESOURCE`, `WORKSPACE`, `INTEGRATION_TARGET`, `GIT_INTEGRATION_ON_DISK`, `ARTIFACT_OBJECT_STAGING`; freeze the seven design populations and the explicit class-to-population rows, with only the provider class containing two populations. Define closed proof/truth/disposition/result vocabularies, precise mapping error codes (`RECOVERY_INVENTORY_CLASS_EXTRA|UNKNOWN|DUPLICATE|OMITTED`), coordinator `UNKNOWN_TRUTH`, layer `RECOVERY_INVENTORY`, ledger upstream codes/layer, bounds, and immutable record/input/result types. Model terminal cancellation explicitly without granting retry/history authority; do not let Git/submodule evidence certify durable integration attempts or artifact-object evidence certify scheduler resources.
implementationPlan.note:
Contract hardened for the rejection. Frozen class/population mapping, vocabularies and bounds are unchanged (6 classes / 7 populations / provider class shared).

Added: five reason codes to the closed upstream vocabulary — RECOVERY_INVENTORY_PROOF_CLASS_EXTRA / _UNKNOWN / _DUPLICATE, RECOVERY_INVENTORY_PROOF_DIGEST_RESERVED, RECOVERY_INVENTORY_ITEM_PROOF_MISMATCH — distinct from the four CLASS_* codes so a green test can name which guard refused. Added RECOVERY_UNKNOWN_PROOF_DIGEST as the shared reserved sentinel (was a private const in record.ts; the codec now needs it to re-derive the unbacked-slot invariant).

Proxy containment: new isReflectableObject() and isPlainArray() ask types.isProxy FIRST — before Array.isArray, before any descriptor read — and exactDataRecord now routes through them. That closes both escapes measured in step 1: the throwing-ownKeys proxy that escaped as Error('trap-executed') and the revoked proxy that escaped as TypeError from Array.isArray. Transparent proxies are refused categorically because a proxy target can be swapped between two reads.

implementationPlan.description: Implement total record normalization/adjudication and its exact LF bridge. Validate hostile inputs with own enumerable data descriptors before property access; require the exact configured six-class set and normalize a missing/incomplete configured proof into its canonical UNKNOWN proof slot rather than shrinking the mapping. Bind each subject to its one mapped proof, project/project-tag, verified backup cursor+generation, selected anchor binding digest/incarnation/key epoch, source proof digest, restored-intent reference/digest, terminal proof or quarantine reference, disposition, and separate coordinator/upstream refusal tuples. Enforce: ABSENT only from complete negative proof; CANCELLED only from terminal cancellation proof; ADOPTED only when external/restored identity and both selected recovery refs match exactly; unmatched items only QUARANTINED or UNKNOWN; any incomplete/non-fenceable/artifact-or-key/unresolved fact makes the persisted truth `UNKNOWN_TRUTH`/`RECOVERY_INVENTORY`. Deep-freeze copied data and expose no secret/message bytes.
implementationPlan.note:
Record normalization/adjudication rebuilt around the two provenance gaps.

NEW MODULE recovery-inventory-proofs.ts (154 lines) + exact LF .js bridge — the configured-proof side, split out of record.ts to hold the per-file target (record.ts is now 210 lines, down from 244 with the new logic added):
- indexConfiguredProofs() validates the supplied ROWS as a closed unique set instead of consulting them with supplied.find. Length is asked FIRST (with only six class names an over-long list is always also a duplicate, so the EXTRA branch would otherwise be unreachable for every input — the same trap already recorded on refuseConfiguredClasses). Unknown class -> PROOF_CLASS_UNKNOWN, repeat -> PROOF_CLASS_DUPLICATE, over-length -> PROOF_CLASS_EXTRA, reserved sentinel digest -> PROOF_DIGEST_RESERVED. An OMITTED row stays legitimate: it is the canonical UNKNOWN slot.
- refuseContradictingProof() cross-links every subject to the one proof of its mapped class; a subject citing a digest its class proof contradicts is a structural refusal (ITEM_PROOF_MISMATCH), because the caller supplied a fact and a proof that cannot both be true.
- unbackedItem() downgrades an item whose class has no configured proof to UNKNOWN with retained RECOVERY_INVENTORY_PROOF_MISSING provenance — the item keeps its own reported digest, nothing is restamped, and no unbacked evidence can hold a positive disposition.
- normaliseProofs() moved here unchanged in behaviour, now keyed off the validated index.

recovery-inventory-subject.ts: readEvidence() asks isReflectableObject first (its `kind` peek is itself a reflective read that a trap would beat), and readArray() uses isPlainArray so a revoked proxy refuses instead of throwing from Array.isArray.

Two pre-existing FIXTURE defects surfaced and were fixed, both of which had been masking the missing invariant: the ledger fixture built subject digests from the POPULATION index while proofs used the CLASS index (7 populations over 6 classes, so 5 of 7 subjects cited a proof digest that was not theirs), and the record test's digest-binding case moved a proof digest without its items.

Fresh focused run: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/recovery/recovery-inventory -> 3 files, 60 passed (60). typecheck exits 0.

implementationPlan.description: Implement the strict canonical codec and exact LF bridge. Encode a versioned, fixed-key-order, bounded UTF-8 JSON body with deterministic class/population/item ordering; compute SHA-256 over every body field except `recordDigest`, then append that digest. Decode with fatal UTF-8, exact keys/vocabularies/bounds/cardinalities, re-derived six-to-seven mapping and disposition invariants, digest recomputation, and byte-for-byte canonical re-encoding so whitespace, key order, duplicate keys, extensions, truncation, or any semantic byte mutation cannot become an alternate authoritative record. Return the stable unreadable upstream code/layer under coordinator UNKNOWN rather than throwing or defaulting.
implementationPlan.note:
Codec now RE-DERIVES the item-to-proof provenance link on decode instead of trusting stored rows, closing the readback half of the rejected gap: a forged record whose digest was recomputed over the forgery would otherwise decode as authoritative.

Inside readRecord, alongside the existing per-class itemCount check and AHEAD of the digest comparison and the canonical re-encode:
- when a proof slot carries a real digest, every item of that class must cite exactly that digest;
- when a proof slot carries the reserved RECOVERY_UNKNOWN_PROOF_DIGEST sentinel (no configured proof), every item of that class must be disposition UNKNOWN — a terminal or adopted disposition under an unbacked slot is refused.
Both answer RECOVERY_INVENTORY_RECORD_NONCANONICAL at RECOVERY_INVENTORY under coordinator UNKNOWN_TRUTH; nothing throws and nothing defaults.

Guard ORDER is asserted, not assumed: the hardening test that tampers one item digest expects RECORD_NONCANONICAL and would have received RECORD_DIGEST_MISMATCH had the structural check run after the digest check. Encoding, key order, bounds and the fatal-UTF-8 path are unchanged. codec.ts is 331 lines (+10), under the 400 cap. Focused run: 60 passed (60); daemon typecheck exits 0.

implementationPlan.description: Implement content-addressed durable persistence/readback and its exact LF bridge using only the existing public `SqliteEventStore` transaction surface—no schema change or raw SQLite. The write service must read the fixed ACTIVE recovery binding from the project store and the exact anchored incarnation, cross-check key epoch/project/backup generation, and only then build the record; it must accept no request-selected current refs. Commit canonical bytes once under a domain-separated record-digest aggregate with command kind `recovery.reconcile_external`, expectedVersion 0, exact domain schema/event IDs, and identical request/result/event bytes; exact retries replay one event. The reader addresses an explicit record digest (never an invented 'latest'), verifies the sole sequence-1 event plus decision trace/decision bytes and codec/digest/aggregate identity, and maps absent, conflicting, malformed, or unverifiable evidence to `UNKNOWN_TRUTH`/`RECOVERY_INVENTORY` while retaining `RECORD_NOT_FOUND|UNREADABLE|CONFLICT` at `RECOVERY_INVENTORY_LEDGER`. R3 may later bind this immutable digest; this task grants no recovery.complete authority.
implementationPlan.note:
Durable persistence production code is unchanged — it still reads the ACTIVE binding and anchored incarnation from the store, accepts no request-selected refs, commits once under the domain-separated record-digest aggregate at expectedVersion 0, and reads back only by an explicit digest. What changed is that it now INHERITS the two new provenance guards, and that is proved at the ledger surface rather than assumed from the builder's unit tests.

New case "persists nothing when supplied provenance contradicts itself": a positive control commits the untouched facts first (so the refusals below cannot be blamed on the binding, the anchor, or a malformed fixture), then a 2-case sweep (swept===2) drives recordRecoveryReconciliation with (a) one subject digest mutated to deadbeef... and (b) a seventh-class 'ALIEN' proof row, asserting exact upstream RECOVERY_INVENTORY_ITEM_PROOF_MISMATCH / RECOVERY_INVENTORY_PROOF_CLASS_UNKNOWN at RECOVERY_INVENTORY, coordinator UNKNOWN_TRUTH, authority NONE.

Also fixed in step 4 and load-bearing here: the ledger fixture itself had been building subject digests off the population index, so 5 of its 7 subjects cited a proof digest that was not their class's — the durable sink had been committing self-contradictory provenance in every one of its own green tests.

Fresh: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck exits 0; focused recovery-inventory run 3 files / 61 passed (61). No schema change, no raw SQLite, no 'latest' pointer, no recovery.complete authority.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: SEVEN PROOF ROWS — rejected: it duplicates the one combined runner proof merely to inflate cardinality. FIVE PROOFS BY FOLDING DURABLE INTEGRATION INTO GIT — rejected: the landed Git adapter proves refs/submodules, not durable integration attempts. FOLDING RESOURCE INTO ARTIFACT — rejected: object/staging enumeration is not scheduler resource authority. EXTENDING THE RUNNER CLASS UNION/COLLECTOR — rejected: its four node-side classes are already a closed, focused 378-line aggregate and task-47 is allowed to deliver two daemon typed proof bridges without reversing dependency direction. A CUSTOM SQLITE TABLE — rejected: the existing expected-version decision/event transaction provides replay, reopen, and strict readback without shared-schema churn. A MUTABLE 'LATEST' RECORD — rejected as unspecified authority: records are immutable/content-addressed and the later R3 decision binds an explicit digest. ONLY FOUR DISPOSITIONS — rejected as a narrowing of the pinned design, whose line 978 explicitly distinguishes terminal cancellation; CANCELLED is therefore represented as a proof-bearing, zero-retry terminal disposition alongside the four task-named values.

planningNotes.risks: The runner registration factories preserve only aggregate inventory code/layer, not the deeper Git/artifact observer refusal; retain exactly what production exposes and never invent deeper provenance. `readCurrentRecoveryAuthenticationBinding` collapses missing/unreadable to null, so the ledger must fail closed with a local upstream code rather than claim a selected binding.
